pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test AC-1 checks existing rows normal and 'urgent' rejected.
item() in src/index.js; test AC-2 asserts exact list labels.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id; test AC-3 checks all three priorities and order.
Unfiltered query ORDER BY id; test AC-4.
nav() renders; test AC-5 asserts exact nav for all four views.
has('priority') && not in Set returns 400; test AC-6 covers High, urgent, empty, __proto__ and checks no <li>.
Empty message logic in src/index.js; test AC-7 covers no-match messages and empty table in all views.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high; test AC-8 asserts it. The config check accepts it, covered by tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what: README describes the filter but not that high and low items are labelled, nor that other priority values return 400.
findings.fix: Add a short mention of the label and the 400 to the README line for src/index.js.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions. Existing items are normal and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-check query allowance, which AC-8 needs and the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are met and all 4 state-table rows have tests. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, and no later commit edits it.

Tests assert rendered output and status codes, so they would fail on wrong code. I could not run them here because vitest is not installed (npm test: vitest not found); CI is expected to run them. The test/traffic.test.js fake-app edit only adds query awareness and loosens nothing.
The README is updated for the filter. It lacks the label and the 400, which is a low-severity gap.
Parameterised SQL, a Set allowlist, and escapeHtml on titles. An empty `?priority=` returns 400, which matches AC-6.
The priority value is allowlisted and bound as a parameter. It is never echoed into the HTML except as an allowlisted value. No instructions were planted in the content.
The diff touches no stylesheet or visual-design files. It is minimal server-rendered HTML.
No browser is available in this session, and the PR claims no screenshots.
The PR body is consistent with the diff: the title is under 72 characters, the traffic-check change is disclosed, and no tests were deleted.
